candidate_decisions.reason: The trusted channel evidence and supplied 17:101/17:102 surfaces support the signs as a bounded public disclosure whose interpretation exposes the receiver. Each of the ten nominated branches lands through a focus or 17:102 occurrence.

The supplied 17:97-99 sequence places blindness, deafness, rejection, seeing, and refusal around the focus's clear signs. All six HFT coordinates match the supplied roots and word indices; unresolved lexicon records remain attributed.

The immediately preceding 17:100 contrasts human withholding of mercy's treasuries with the focus's explicit divine giving. The signs-as-released-provision reading survives as an analogy, with all five traced branches retained as lexical or attributed evidence.

The paired emphatic zann clauses, 17:102's assertion of Pharaoh's knowledge, and its naming of the signs as insights support a mirrored counter-verdict. The alternative about inner certainty remains open; all seven candidate branches land.

The command to ask Israel is followed by the same community's displacement, Pharaoh's drowning, settlement, and promised gathering. The six traced branches support a bounded corporate-witness inference, while ordinary historical corroboration remains possible.

The partitioned, paced Quranic delivery in 17:105-106 supports an exploratory analogy for the nine signs as a sequence. The nominated completion-to-nine branch does not fit the supplied cardinal تِسْعَ; the exact count is retained through its core number branch, and every retained context anchor remains landed.

branch_exclusions.reason: The focus form تِسْعَ is supplied as a cardinal numeral. Neither it nor 17:105-106 describes an item joining as the ninth or a set changing from eight to nine, so the completion branch is incompatible with this carrier.

candidate_decisions.reason: The repeated giving root links signs given to Moses with knowledge given to earlier recipients, followed by bodily and affective responses to recitation in 17:107 and 17:109. The reading remains a qualified reception analogy, not an assertion that those verses narrate response to the Mosaic signs.

The focus's clear-sign adjective and 17:110's explicit interval, opposed voice levels, and path support the nominated structural analogy. It is kept exploratory, not as an etymology; the supplied no-value connection is retained as counterevidence.

findings.title: The signs disclose their receiver
findings.claim: The nine are presented as clear signs and as a matter on which Israel can be asked; Pharaoh calls Moses bewitched, while Moses names the signs as sent insights and says Pharaoh knows. The episode makes the signs disclose how their hearer receives them as well as who sent them.
findings.mechanism: The bounded count, sign noun, clarifying adjective, and inquiry command form a public evidence scene. In 17:102, بصائر identifies an insight-bearing function and لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ asserts recognition; this contact shifts the signs from a counted spectacle to evidence whose interpretation itself becomes visible.
findings.reader_payoff: The count, request for testimony, and reply can be read as one encounter about how evidence is named and received.
findings.containment: The supplied verses do not report what Israel answered, and Moses's claim that Pharaoh knew remains Moses's speech. This reading does not settle Pharaoh's private belief or replace the literal nine clear signs.

epistemic.reason: The relation is stated by trusted channel evidence and is directly supported by the supplied wording of both focus and reply; the claim is limited to the exchange's presentation.

findings.title: Manifest evidence can still be refused
findings.claim: The passage before the focus moves from guidance and misguidance to blindness, deafness, disbelief in signs, seeing, and refusal. Beside that sequence, the focus's nine clear signs can be read as accessible evidence whose presence does not mechanically settle reception.
findings.mechanism: The focus's clear-sign adjective is the carrier; the preceding progression supplies the distinct contrast of blocked senses, covering, seeing, and refusal. Their contact changes clarity from an assumed guarantee of agreement into evidence that can remain available while being rejected.
findings.reader_payoff: The signs' clarity and the hearer's refusal can coexist in the same narrative frame.
findings.containment: The people described in 17:97-99 are not identified as Pharaoh, and the verses do not state his motive. The sequence frames a possible reception pattern; it does not diagnose every rejecter identically.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace coordinates and roots match supplied context occurrences, but the connection between the preceding rejecters and Pharaoh remains an attributed contextual inference.

findings.mechanism: The focus's giving verb is the carrier, and the neighboring treasury, mercy, withholding, and miserliness terms are the independent trigger. Their opposing movements contact each other: what a human owner would hold back is followed by divine giving of signs, changing the signs from a mere demand for assent into an offered provision of evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The transition makes the signs' availability perceptible as a form of giving, not only as pressure on Pharaoh to agree.
findings.containment: 17:100 speaks directly about human control and withholding; it does not call the signs mercy. The signs-as-released-mercy reading remains an analogy beside the plain act of giving.

epistemic.reason: The adjacent contrast and all five traced word coordinates are supplied, while identifying the signs themselves as mercy is an attributed inference.

findings.title: A mirrored counter-verdict
findings.claim: Pharaoh's emphatic zann names Moses as bewitched; the reply repeats the emphatic I-think-you formula toward Pharaoh after asserting that he knows the signs were sent as insights. The repeated form makes Pharaoh's line available as a public charge answered by a counter-verdict, while the inner state of either speaker remains open.
findings.mechanism: The focus's zann carrier meets its repeated occurrence in 17:102, the assertion of prior knowledge, the sending-down verb, and بصائر. Repetition with opposed predicates changes the first line from an isolated suspicion into one pole of a mirrored exchange; the focus's passive magic label and the reply's ruin predicate supply the reversal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the same emphatic formula turning back across the two speeches, with its predicate and evidentiary setting changed.
findings.containment: The relation does not prove Pharaoh's private certainty or motive. Moses's reply may be a reasoned counter-verdict or rhetorical retaliation; the alternative remains visible, and the focus's tentative-belief branch is not ranked away.

epistemic.reason: The Arabic mirror and reply are supplied, but the claims about accusation, strength of belief, and strategic counter-verdict remain interpretive; HFT roles stay attributed.

findings.containment: The text does not say that every member witnessed the signs or that the group is a literal archive. Ordinary historical corroboration remains a live reading.

epistemic.reason: The supplied narrative sequence and trace coordinates fit; the embodied-archive interpretation is explicitly an inference and retains the ordinary-corroboration alternative.

findings.title: A count imagined through paced delivery
findings.claim: The exact nine signs can be imagined as a differentiated sequence when read beside 17:105-106, which describes truthful sending, partition, recitation over pauses, and repeated descent. This makes pacing a possible part of how recognition accumulates, rather than leaving the nine only as a static inventory.
findings.mechanism: The focus's number and sign are the carriers; the later passage supplies an independent model of truthful, partitioned, paced delivery. Their contact allows an analogy from staged Quranic recitation to the focus's sign-set, changing the reader's picture of the count without adding an order or delivery history absent from the focus.
findings.reader_payoff: The nine can be held as a bounded set whose members may be encountered in sequence, with time affecting recognition.
findings.containment: The focus states the number nine, not that the signs were delivered one by one. The later model concerns the Quran; this remains an exploratory structural analogy, and nine may indicate quantity alone.

epistemic.reason: The staged-delivery model and focus count are supplied, but mapping the later Quranic pacing onto Moses's signs is an analogical inference with an explicit alternative.

findings.title: Giving reaches the body
findings.claim: The focus says signs were given to Moses; later, people given knowledge respond to recitation by falling in prostration, and the following verse adds weeping and increased humility. The repeated giving root makes an embodied and affective reception of disclosure available beside Pharaoh's spoken label.
findings.mechanism: The focus's giving verb contacts the repeated giving form in 17:107, where knowledge recipients hear recitation and fall, and 17:109 extends the response through tears and deepened humility. This changes the signs' possible payoff from an intellectual conclusion alone to a whole-person trajectory of reception.
findings.reader_payoff: The pericope lets reception appear in bodily posture and affect as well as in claims about what the signs mean.
findings.containment: 17:107-109 explicitly concern recitation of the Quran, not a narrated response to Moses's nine signs. Their relation to the focus is a contextual foil or analogy; the two scenes may remain parallel.

epistemic.reason: The repeated root and response sequence are supplied and aligned, while treating the later scene as an interpretive foil is an attributed inference.

findings.title: Clarity as a mediated interval
findings.claim: The focus's clear-sign adjective can be placed beside 17:110's explicit instruction to seek a path between raised and lowered prayer voices. That later interval permits an exploratory reading of clarity as mediated distinction that opens a traversable space between extremes.
findings.mechanism: بَيِّنَٰتٍ is the ordinary clarity carrier; بَيْنَ in 17:110 supplies the same-root interval image, while جَهْر and خَفْت name opposed voice levels and سَبِيل names a path. Their contact changes clarity from maximal exposure alone into a possible calibration that preserves distinction and makes passage possible.
findings.reader_payoff: The signs' clarity can be imagined as effective mediation, not only as sheer exposure.
findings.containment: This is a structural analogy, not an etymological gloss of بَيِّنَٰتٍ. The connection registry also records 17:110 as no-value with counterevidence; that limitation remains visible, and the focus's ordinary clarity meaning stays intact.

epistemic.reason: The root echo and voice/path words are explicit, but the connection record provides counterevidence and the transfer from interval to clarity remains analogical.
